# Results — Study 776 (Valentine-Sparkle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Signet Jewelers (SIG) rallies into Valentine's Day**: bid up in the weeks before the
gifting holiday, then fades once it is past. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `55e1ce2a38e2` (SIG + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `SIG` (Signet Jewelers) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 4,652 rows, 2008-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 18 Valentine's Days 2009→2026, each February 14 (fixed by the Gregorian calendar; anchored on the last trading close on/before the 14th when it lands on a weekend) |
| Events resolvable | all **18** of 18 Valentine's Days have SIG+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (SIG − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: Valentine's Day is fixed years ahead. Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; fade = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Beta, named:** SIG is a volatile mid-cap specialty retailer with a market beta well above
1, so a raw `SIG − SPY` difference over any drifting window is partly mechanical. The
run-up/fade windows here are short (2-4 weeks), so beta is a minor contaminant — but it is
the reason we quote the *abnormal* return throughout, never the raw SIG move.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE Valentine's Day (SIG − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 18 | −1.275% | −0.929 | 7/18 = 38.9% [20.3%, 61.4%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 18 | −2.714% | −1.021 | 8/18 = 44.4% [24.6%, 66.3%] |

The bullish folklore is **absent — and if anything mildly inverted**: in the two weeks
*into* Valentine's, SIG has on average *under*-performed SPY by −1.28% (*t* = −0.93), and
over a month by −2.71% (*t* = −1.02). Neither is close to significant, but both point the
*wrong* way for a "rally into the gifting quarter" story. The hit rate is below 50% on both
cuts.

## The fade — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER Valentine's Day

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week fade (k=10) | 18 | +1.137% | +0.516 | 9/18 = 50.0% [29.0%, 71.0%] |
| 1-month fade (k=21) | 18 | +0.869% | +0.224 | 8/18 = 44.4% [24.6%, 66.3%] |

The "sell the holiday" half is a **clean zero, pointing the wrong way**: post-Valentine's
SIG is, if anything, *up* versus SPY (both cuts |*t*| < 0.6) — the opposite of a fade. There
is no reliable post-holiday drop to short.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | −1.275% | +0.469% (2.270%) | 0.786 |
| 2-week fade | left | +1.137% | +0.469% (2.270%) | 0.625 |

Both cuts sit **inside the luck cloud**: the run-up's right-tail p = 0.79 (a random 2-week
window would beat it 79% of the time) and the fade's left-tail p = 0.62. Nothing here is
outside SIG's ordinary tracking noise.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week run-up *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.929**; across all 18 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−1.956, −0.521]** — it never reaches significance in either direction, so there is no
single dominant year to point to and no stable tilt to bank.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | −1.275% (*t* −0.93) | −1.375% (*t* −1.00) | −1.475% (*t* −1.08) |
| 2-week fade | +1.137% (*t* +0.52) | +1.037% (*t* +0.47) | +0.937% (*t* +0.43) |

Costs only push the (insignificant) run-up slightly more negative and the (insignificant)
fade slightly less positive — but neither window ever clears |*t*| = 1.1, so there is
nothing to trade gross *or* net. Even the mildly-negative run-up would only be a *short* of
a −1.3%/yr window 18 times, a capacity-trivial curiosity built on a *t* of −0.93.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.61 (sd 1.49); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **3/20** seeds —
  the honest small-sample false-positive rate at n = 18 events with a 10-day AR (~15%),
  a caution flag that even a |*t*| ~ 2 here would not be conclusive.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 782):** mean AR +0.449%, *t* = **+0.52**.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 782):** mean AR +1.449%, *t* = **+1.68** — a real bump is
  recovered monotonically, confirming the detector fires when there *is* something to find.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | No rally into Valentine's and no fade after. Every window is insignificant (2wk run-up −1.28%, *t* = −0.93; 1mo run-up −2.71%, *t* = −1.02; both fades |*t*| < 0.6), the placebo sits dead in the luck cloud (right-tail p = 0.79), the jackknife *t* never leaves [−1.96, −0.52], and the synthetic null itself fires |*t*| ≥ 2 on 3/20 seeds at this n. The point estimates even lean the *wrong* way for the folklore. Indistinguishable from noise. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. No window clears |*t*| = 1.1 gross or net; the only faintly-directional cut is a short of a −1.3%/yr window on a single volatile mid-cap 18 times — capacity-trivial, statistically empty, and inside a 4-window multiple-testing search. |

**In one sentence:** the "buy the jeweller into Valentine's Day" trade is folklore twice
over — Signet does *not* rally into February 14 (if anything it drifts mildly *below* SPY)
and it does *not* fade after; every cut is inside the noise, so there is nothing to trade.
